newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Rosneft sees 51 pct sale in smaller stakes.
newsitem.headline: Russia Rosneft sees 51 pct sale in smaller stakes.

text.p: Russian oil company Rosneft hopes a 51 percent stake in its shares will be broken up and sold in smaller stakes, a spokesman said on Monday.

"If the stake is broken up, the price of each portion sold could be higher because a blocking or controlling stake will have to be built up," said Vladimir Vyunitsky, press secretary to Rosneft's chief executive, Yuri Bespalov.
Vyunitsky did not say whether the company had a say in how the stake, which is due to be sold at a cash auction this year, perhaps as early as September, would be sold off.
The head of the State Property Committee, which is responsible for such sales, said last week that over 90 percent of Rosneft might be sold off this year.

Vyunitsky said the timing of the sale of the second stake (about 41.4 percent of shares) would be coordinated with the property committee and the Russian Federal Property Fund to ensure the value of the stake was not reduced by selling at a time when the market was oversupplied with shares in oil companies.
He said Bespalov thought the company ought to receive no less than $500 million from the sale of the 41.4 percent stake.
"On this, we're counting not so much on getting money as on potential strategic investors getting the shares," Vyunitsky said.

Rosneft is one of a series of major Russian companies which the government is partially privatising in a drive to raise much needed cash to fill a gaping budget hole and pay trillions of roubles in overdue wages.
